title: TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement)
summary: A three-hour self-improvement live Q&A covering confrontation, willpower, loneliness, porn, discipline, charisma, boundaries, masculinity, Nietzsche and dealing with family and negative people. Training comes up as an analogy and in a few practical answers: low-volume heavy work for manual laborers, short morning sessions for people with long shifts, rebuilding work capacity gradually, and saving music for hard sets.
claims: He doesn't do seated meditation; walking for two hours in the forest without a single thought is his meditation
He openly prioritizes his arms over his shoulders
It is better to live with remorse than with regret: acting and failing beats inaction, because you can apologize and grow from a mistake
Rejection stings at first but means nothing a year later; being turned down by 20-40 women made him comfortable with rejection and more proactive
He still has imposter syndrome on YouTube and reminds himself not to over-justify everything he says
Fear of confrontation often comes from a childhood sheltered from conflict; fix it by micro-dosing low-stakes confrontations to train your psyche
He routinely confronts queue-cutters and has never been hit for it, even when he was smaller and weaker
A good father leads by example: treat the children's mother tenderly to model how a man treats a woman, and let the kids see you train so they want to be disciplined like you
In grad school, while working and teaching, he wrote a daily paper list of tasks; going to bed with an item undone counted as failure
People whose parents taught them discipline in school do well at university, where intelligence alone is no longer enough
If a job you hate makes life feel pointless, find meaning outside it: a hobby, a skill to master, or someone in your life
If you only feel good while training and the depression returns afterwards, you are in a gymcel cycle; the solution lies elsewhere
Willpower is finite but trainable; every time you give in to a temptation like Nutella you teach yourself your will is weak, and every resistance strengthens it
Will is largely a psychological construct: people with the most will have convinced themselves they have it (Nietzsche's weak will vs strong will)
Don't let your brain rationalize away remorse; personal shame shows you broke your own principles and must do better
Loneliness is your own responsibility; start conversations with baristas, people at the library, or someone at the gym wearing a band shirt you like
Organic communities like the church are gone, so you must create your own third spaces
To learn French: grind the grammar first, then children's cartoons, then Le Petit Prince, plus daily Duolingo for at least an hour; you have to love it because it's hardly worth it
Monk mode only suits people who lack individuation; isolation makes most people worse, and his own instinct to isolate has never helped him
David Goggins proves it's never too late to change, but don't follow his hypertrophy advice
Since age three he has been happy alone for hours; he sits at the extreme low end of social need
To quit porn: make a pact with yourself, put parental controls on your devices with someone you trust holding the password, and think about the consequences like a smoker looking at lung cancer
Porn is designed to be irresistible, damages your capacity for a relationship with a good woman, and keeps getting more extreme; it is one of the most important self-improvement issues today
Link training and studying: in high school he did homework then push-ups, sit-ups and curls; e.g. 45 min of homework, then some exercises
Ring dips are not better for hypertrophy; regular dips on a dip station are good
Dark thoughts and suicidal ideation are rooted in a distorted view of yourself; you need people who can give an outside perspective, or a hotline
Following Nietzsche, he chooses to believe 100% in free will: whatever you can control is your responsibility, and an external locus of control is an excuse
Start Nietzsche with Beyond Good and Evil alongside his video series
Growing up in a religious cult that crushes individuality requires patience and resisting their guilt-based manipulation; they are the crazy ones, not you
The pathological stoic who represses all emotion cuts himself off from himself; manosphere voices wrongly equate self-improvement with becoming a statue
Jack Hanma in Baki embodies the PED-user mindset: living only in the present and sacrificing his future, and he loses because of it; he's not a role model
Worst self-improvement advice: suppress emotions, and chase material things like sports cars and watches; it makes you a consumerist drone and attracts leeches
Most materialist self-improvement gurus got rich off their followers, not hard work; it's a Ponzi scheme men fall for
Charisma basics: eye contact, posture, good hygiene, practising public speaking, and above all not caring what others think; attractiveness drives perceived charisma
Build a daily routine from small fragmented tasks: start with a shower, then dishes, then harder items; like warming up before a top deadlift set
Surround yourself with go-getters rather than complainers; French whining culture drags people down, which is part of why he left France
In France being muscular attracts constant negative remarks; in high school he refused classmates' drinking invitations to go train instead
To stop feeling not good enough: quit social media, especially Instagram, pinpoint the insecurity and become excellent at it; self-love must be earned
He hated himself as a small, weak young man; it took about five years of training to wake up in a body he loved
Training is not an act of faith but an act of worship of the body (cf. Mishima's Sun and Steel)
Nothing happening more than 50 km from you matters for your self-improvement; quitting news costs you nothing
He is agnostic and spiritual; training is his way of worshipping nature, and his core rule is that whatever expands you is good and whatever shrinks you is bad
The ancient Greeks never separated mind and body (Plato means wide shoulders; philosophers wrestled for hours); seeing bodybuilding as spiritual keeps you going when results slow
Spending time on yourself isn't selfish; you are the most important person in your life until you have kids
A real identity stands on its own; an identity borrowed from a group is a mask
Limits are mostly self-inflicted; he keeps pushing mind and body and hasn't seen his limit; people who claim to have hit theirs have hit mediocrity
At 16 he wrote a 15-page essay on Rousseau including a psychoanalysis of him and got 5/20 from a teacher who loved Rousseau
Gender is a social construct built on real biology that historically organized society; whether it is still needed should be judged through individuation
For women to be taken seriously in the gym: dress to train, train hard, politely shut down approaches, and pick a hardcore gym where people come to train
He cares little about money: enough to provide for his family plus some savings; don't take finance advice from him
Short height is a filter that repels vain women; he was once short and knows how badly short men are treated
Porn addiction is the hardest to quit because access is so easy, so restricting access is essential; the porn industry is human trafficking at scale
Lifting won't win a fight; men should get baseline striking and some wrestling (boxing, savate, muay thai, wrestling) and avoid ground arts like BJJ or judo for the street
Work capacity rebuilds gradually, like training volume: you can't jump from 9 to 16 sets or double volume at once without wrecking yourself for days
For manual laborers: high intensity, minimal volume and fairly low frequency, e.g. two heavy sets of a compound instead of four to eight, so the gym doesn't hurt your job
Feeling a cold coming, he ate raw garlic and trained, and felt better the next day
Social anxiety is a phobia treated by gradual exposure; in 2019 three people in a house made him panic, now he can spend 5 hours with 20 strangers; it took about three years
As a teen he obsessively feared smelling and kept reapplying deodorant, which isolated him; he then went deliberately hypersocial
Masculinity is a social construct that exists to complement femininity: physical and mental strength, emotional steadiness, providing, shouldering more and not complaining
Family is the number one factor that can hinder personal development; he only started building himself up once he left home
Don't fear post-graduation life: his working years gave him more freedom than grad school because weekends are his own
The grind-first-then-relationships discourse is dangerous; most people can do both, unless you're building a family
There is no point where effort yields nothing, so cosmetic surgery is a cop-out; he learned to love his big nose. Exceptions are loose skin and gynecomastia
Many people who get one cosmetic surgery go on to get more (he cites roughly 75% getting a second)
Kindness is finite: give it to those who are kind to you; boundaries are non-negotiable; start enforcing them with family, then strangers
Nietzsche's eternal recurrence is the best self-improvement exercise: live as though you'll relive this exact life forever; only actions count, not intentions
The Übermensch is defined by creating his own values, not strength, and is an unreachable ideal; will to power drives every living being
Journey to the West's Sun Wukong is the original male power fantasy and the root of most anime and manga
Job hunting: in 2018 he sent 100 applications for about 8 callbacks and 1 job; apply everywhere and ignore listed requirements
For someone working 60-70 h/week: don't train on 16-hour shift days, train in the morning before work; 30 minutes gets you 4-5 hard sets, and 2 hours a week is already a lot; prioritize rest
He has never used dating apps; they favour women and reward only the most attractive men
Work is an obligation; find a job you can tolerate; he refuses to monetize his passion to protect it
His Dune video took about 20 hours of writing, 7-8 hours of recording and 12 hours of editing
Fear of judgment comes from deriving self-worth from others; the average person is not worth using as your mirror
He knew he was an adult when he bused 45 minutes to buy groceries with his own money and cooked chicken himself
Training is non-negotiable for everyone, but bodybuilding is a personal choice; if you hate the gym, try martial arts
Living with your parents to save money while contributing is the ideal situation, not unmanly
He has lost a parent; you can't prepare for it, so call your parents and tell them you love them
He hasn't been back to France in about seven years
One morning coffee is a ritual, not an addiction; coffee all day long is what sustains the addiction
He quit video games about 11 years ago because of his addictive personality and has not played since
Cynicism is a cop-out that robs you of joy; he dislikes that trait in himself
Before getting frustrated with human limits, get to a 10-plate dip
To train aggressively: no phone; between sets stare at the floor or ceiling and think about the next set
He almost never trains to music: 95% of sessions are podcasts or classical music; save bangers for hard sets so you don't desensitize, like with caffeine
Listening to music all day is an addiction and a sign you can't stand your own thoughts
Procrastination: start with small steps so small rewards condition you; stop waiting for one big transformation day
Test new principles by living them; if others push back, it often means you're on the right path
Self-improvement talk can become addictive motivation without action; always apply
Adjustable dumbbells are a trap: expensive base and plates; only buy if you'll use them at least three times a week
Nietzsche's God is dead is a diagnosis of society, not a celebration; many viewers returned to their faith after his Nietzsche videos
At a very progressive university he was ostracized for speaking his mind and is glad he did
Shyness is fear of revealing who you are; introversion is a separate trait about social energy
Start philosophy with the Stoics (Seneca, Marcus Aurelius), not Mishima's abstract Sun and Steel
His wife made him less rigid; he used to panic when his schedule broke; discipline can become a straitjacket
Random anger bursts usually come from trauma; physical bullying when young means he still goes into fight mode when someone shoves or slaps him
Teach discipline early: it gives kids a huge advantage, and it's much harder to build when you're older
He has a strongly avoidant attachment style and improved it by telling loved ones what bothered him instead of withdrawing
Modern shonen heroes are crybabies (male weakness fantasies), unlike the hypermasculine 80s-90s heroes; he would show his sons Dragon Ball Z
You can't help people who don't want help; they'll drag you down like a drowning person
Discipline isn't one-to-one transferable: like lift carryover, you still have to train the specific area you want to improve, e.g. social life
Helplessness is learned, like Corkus in Berserk who believes only special people control their fate
Throw out deadlines for self-improvement goals; e.g. aim for a 5-plate dip whenever it comes, so you don't build resentment toward yourself
Teach kids discipline by making it a game, e.g. 20 minutes of chess study a day so they win more
